Middle East.headline: ‘All I want to do is cry’: trauma of 7 October survivors three years after the attacks
Middle East.body: Israeli communities shattered by Hamas massacres are torn between rebuilding their lives and remembering lost friends and relatives Keith Siegel spent many of his long hours in Hamas captivity in Gaza etching everything that happened after 7 October 2023 into his memory. For 484 days, he recited to himself every place he was held, the dates he was moved and every attack or humiliation he endured or witnessed. He aimed to store intelligence that could help Israeli forces free other hostages if he was released, to keep track of time as the days slid by and be able to tell his family what happened to him. Now his body is free, but he cannot loosen those memories. Continue reading...

Americas.headline: Deadly Colombia earthquake leaves widespread destruction
Americas.body: Deadly Colombia earthquake leaves widespread destruction A 7.4-magnitude earthquake has hit Colombia, killing more than 100 people and damaging thousands of buildings. As rescue teams search for survivors, international aid has begun to arrive. Devastating damage The major earthquake that shook western Colombia on Monday was felt as far away as Ecuador, Venezuela and Panama. According to the US Geological Survey, the quake struck at around 7:34 a.m. local time near San Jose del Palmar in the Choco region, about 400 kilometers (250 miles) west of the capital, Bogota. Africa.headline: Outbreak of deadly Ebola strain with no cure spreads to another country
Africa.body: A Kenyan man died after travelling to Nairobi from the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where a deadly outbreak of Ebola is spreading. Kenya’s health minister, Aden Duale, said the man boarded a flight on Saturday and was screened at the airport before being taken to the hospital. The patient fell ill a month ago and had received treatment in multiple hospitals while he lived in the DRC. The man had travelled from the DRC to Uganda’s capital, where he caught a flight to Nairobi. After being transferred into isolation at a hospital, he tested positive for the deadly virus and died on Monday. The most recent outbreak was declared on May 15.

Africa.headline: Inside the study for a remedy to fight Congo's deadliest Ebola outbreak
Africa.body: RWAMPARA, Congo (AP) — More than 250 participants have been enrolled in a trial for a drug that could stop them from contracting Ebola in Congo, in what experts have described as a critical step to try to fight the deadliest outbreak of the disease in the Central African country. The drug is targeted at Bundibugyo virus, which is responsible for the fast-moving outbreak and is without an approved vaccine or treatment. The trial began in July and is one of several studies launched to find some protection and another way of at least slowing the outbreak. Story continues below video Welcome to the discussion. Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar's Health System Is Under Siege, Endangering the Region
Asia-Pacific.body: On September 28, 2026, an estimated 50 people were killed at a busy market in the western part of Myanmar during an attack by the country's military regime. This attack marks some of the latest violence in a civil war that began in 2021 following a coup by the junta, which overthrew democratically elected leaders. The war has destroyed the health-care system, allowing dangerous diseases to spread, including ones that had all but been eliminated in the country, such as cholera. The international community has neglected the country repeatedly, cutting millions of dollars in aid. Early in the war, it appeared that a coalition of antijunta forces was going to win. Asia-Pacific.headline: A ray of hope amid armed conflict and floods
Asia-Pacific.body: A ray of hope amid armed conflict and floods Delivering safe water and essential hygiene supplies to the crisis affected families in Myanmar “We didn’t have a second to waste. I held my youngest son, who has a disability, close to my chest, grabbed my eldest son’s hand, and we hurried toward higher ground, my heart pounding.” When the flood hit, Nilar Win knew the top priority was getting to safety as fast as her family could, all while keeping her two sons secure. At just 23 years old, Nilar Win lives in the Taung Baw Gar area of Dawei Zay Ward in Sagaing Town, where she and her family face hardship with remarkable resilience.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Nepal seeks China nod to reopen Tatopani border after floods
Asia-Pacific.body: Nepal seeks China nod to reopen Tatopani border after floods Nepal is in talks with China to resume transport services through Tatopani and restore Rasuwagadhi operations. The push underscores how floods, landslides and the August 26 disaster have disrupted Himalayan trade links. Nepal is in talks with China to resume transport services through the Tatopani border point, which has remained closed after recent floods and landslides, Infrastructure Development Minister Sunil Lamsal has said. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Detained immigrants at Georgia ICE facility launch mass hunger strike
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: At least 73 people estimated to have joined protest against prolonged detention and Folkston facility’s ‘violations’ A group of people detained inside a privately-run Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) jail in Georgia have launched a mass hunger strike this week to protest against their prolonged detention and the facility’s conditions, according to advocates and family members. Advocates estimate at least 73 detained immigrants are participating in the hunger strike inside the Folkston D Ray James ICE processing center in south-east Georgia. The Folkston facility, a former state prison, is run by the private prison company GEO Group under a contract with ICE. Continue reading...
